positions.subject: q:housing/transit-oriented-upzoning
positions.summary: Becerra's housing platform says his administration will expand by-right approvals near jobs and transit and build on SB 79 by seeking to end exclusionary zoning around more types of transit.

citations.quote: My administration will pursue zoning reform, expand by-right approvals near jobs and transit, and improve the laws allowing entry-level ownership options like duplexes and small condos.
citations.locator: Policy Agenda, Reform Zoning to Unlock Housing Supply

citations.quote: my administration will build off the success of SB 79 by seeking to end exclusionary zoning around more types of transit and in high-opportunity areas, where children have access to the best schools.

positions.subject: q:immigration/expand-cooperation-federal-enforcement
positions.summary: At the Sept. 30 CNN debate, Becerra referred to California's sanctuary law and criticized Hilton for saying he would enforce Trump's laws but not the state's laws.

citations.quote: Becerra referenced California's sanctuary law, which prohibits local law enforcement from using resources for immigration enforcement.

"You seem to welcome immigrants who look like you but deport immigrants who look like me," Becerra told Hilton. "We need a governor who will protect everyone who works hard. I don't need to be here and listen to you say you'll enforce Trump's laws but not our state laws."

positions.subject: q:taxes/lower-top-income-tax-rates
positions.summary: Becerra endorsed Yes on Proposition 3, which makes the existing income tax rates on high incomes permanent, and at the Sept. 30 debate criticized Hilton's income tax plan as including a tax cut for the wealthiest earners.

citations.quote: YES on Prop 3: The California Children’s Education and Health Care Protection Act of 2026
He pointed out that Hilton’s plan to drop income taxes on the first $150,000 in earnings also includes a tax cut for the state’s wealthiest earners, comparing it to federal tax cuts enacted by Trump.

"Absolutely he's wrong; he would damage the state even harder for working families," Becerra said, arguing the tax cuts would primarily benefit wealthy Californians while reducing funding for schools and healthcare.

positions.subject: q:transportation/high-speed-rail-funding
positions.summary: At a May 2026 campaign stop in Fresno, Becerra said he would scrap the current high-speed rail configuration and make sure the project is finished on budget and on time.

citations.quote: “I’m going to scrap the current configuration, and I’m going to make sure we finish,” Becerra said. “But we’ve got to do it on budget and on time.”

Jonathan Underland, a spokesperson on the Becerra campaign, told Newsweek: "Nearly 80 miles of guideway are complete. The bridges, viaducts, and overpasses are built. The infrastructure is in the ground, and the track is coming. Secretary Becerra is now focused on making sure nothing slows what comes next—cutting through every bottleneck, every broken approval chain, every delay that has held this project back."
